verses.text: Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jucal son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur son of Malchijah heard what Jeremiah was telling all the people:

"This is what the LORD says: 'Whoever stays in this city will die by war, famine, or disease. But whoever goes out and surrenders to the Babylonians will live. They will escape with their life and survive.'
This is what the LORD says: 'This city will certainly be handed over to the army of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.'"

Then the officials said to the king, "This man must be put to death. He is discouraging the soldiers who are left in this city, and all the people too, by the things he is saying. This man is not looking out for the good of these people, but for their harm."
King Zedekiah said, "He is in your hands. The king cannot do anything to stop you."

So they took Jeremiah and threw him into the well of Malchijah, the king's son, which was in the courtyard of the guard. They lowered Jeremiah with ropes. There was no water in the well, only mud, and Jeremiah sank into the mud.
But Ebedmelech the Ethiopian, a court official in the king's palace, heard that they had put Jeremiah into the well. At that time the king was sitting at the Benjamin Gate.
Ebedmelech left the palace and said to the king,

"My lord the king, these men have done a wicked thing in everything they have done to Jeremiah the prophet. They have thrown him into a well, and he will starve to death there, because there is no more bread in the city."
Then the king commanded Ebedmelech the Ethiopian, "Take thirty men from here with you and pull Jeremiah the prophet out of the well before he dies."
So Ebedmelech took the men with him and went to a room under the treasury in the palace. He took some old rags and worn-out clothes from there and lowered them with ropes into the well to Jeremiah.
Ebedmelech the Ethiopian said to Jeremiah, "Put these old rags and worn-out clothes under your arms to pad the ropes." Jeremiah did so.
Then they pulled Jeremiah up with the ropes and lifted him out of the well. And Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard.

Then King Zedekiah sent for the prophet Jeremiah and had him brought to the third entrance of the LORD's temple. The king said to Jeremiah, "I am going to ask you something. Do not hide anything from me."
Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "If I tell you, won't you surely put me to death? And if I give you advice, you will not listen to me."
But King Zedekiah made a secret promise to Jeremiah: "As surely as the LORD lives, who gave us breath, I will not put you to death or hand you over to these men who want to kill you."

Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "This is what the LORD God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: 'If you surrender to the officers of the king of Babylon, your life will be spared and this city will not be burned down. You and your family will live.
But if you do not surrender to the officers of the king of Babylon, this city will be handed over to the Babylonians. They will burn it down, and you will not escape from them.'"
King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "I am afraid of the Jews who have deserted to the Babylonians. They may hand me over to them, and they will treat me cruelly."
But Jeremiah said, "They will not hand you over. Please obey the LORD by doing what I tell you. Then things will go well for you, and your life will be spared.
But if you refuse to surrender, this is what the LORD has shown me:

Look, all the women left in the palace of the king of Judah will be brought out to the officers of the king of Babylon. Those women will say to you: 'Your close friends misled you and overpowered you. Now that your feet are stuck in the mud, they have deserted you.'

All your wives and children will be brought out to the Babylonians. You yourself will not escape from them. You will be captured by the king of Babylon, and this city will be burned down because of you."
Then Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "Do not let anyone know about this conversation, or you will die.
If the officials hear that I talked with you, they may come and say to you, 'Tell us what you said to the king and what the king said to you. Do not hide anything from us, or we will kill you.'
If they do, tell them, 'I was begging the king not to send me back to Jonathan's house to die there.'"
All the officials did come to Jeremiah and question him, and he told them exactly what the king had told him to say. So they said no more to him, because no one had overheard the conversation.
And Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard until the day Jerusalem was captured.
